environment_note: Local macOS CPU run; wall-clock timing must not be generalized across hardware (see docs/research/COMPUTE_ENVIRONMENT.md's methodology warning -- an earlier concurrent two-process run of these same two baselines produced a >5x internally-inconsistent time_select_seconds.txt vs. tqdm/file-mtime elapsed; the runs recorded here were re-executed in isolation, one process at a time, specifically to avoid that confound).

lexrank.note: Re-run in isolation after the scorer_degenerate fix (see docs/research/COMPUTE_ENVIRONMENT.md's 'LexRank 相似度矩陣的已知退化'); an earlier attempt (see evidence_files.f19_lexrank_run_crash_log below) aborted at validation_1082 under the pre-fix fail-loud-and-abort behavior, 36 minutes into a concurrent run alongside textrank, and left no predictions.jsonl artifact at all (write_jsonl_atomic never reached its commit step).

scorer_degenerate_rows.mechanism: length-2 document, zero shared vocabulary between the two sentences -> idf(term)=log(2/2)=0 for every term -> whole similarity matrix collapses to all-zero -> resolved automatically (both sentences fit under budget regardless of ranking)

comparison_table.note: Same denominator (5,621), same evaluate protocol (multisentence_lsum, all-rows default). Lead/Random/system rows are cited from F-16/F-18, not remeasured here.

f19_long_sentence_bias_evidence.hypothesis: sumy TextRank's edge weight (shared-word count / (log(len1)+log(len2))) under-normalizes for sentence length, biasing scores toward longer sentences; sumy LexRank (TF-IDF cosine) has no such coupling.
f19_long_sentence_bias_evidence.conclusion: Hypothesis confirmed quantitatively. This is a faithful property of sumy's implementation of Mihalcea's original TextRank edge weight formula, not a bug in this repo's wiring -- must be documented as a baseline characteristic in the paper.
f19_long_sentence_bias_evidence.downstream_rougeLsum_interpretation: TextRank's lower R-Lsum vs LexRank is consistent with fewer/longer selected sentences reducing per-sentence LCS-matching opportunities -- the same EFFECT CLASS as F-18(a)'s mean-aggregation pathology (greedy+mean's 6.05-sentence collapse), but a DIFFERENT ROOT CAUSE: F-18(a) is a searching objective's aggregation rule triggering early stopping; F-19 is the base scorer itself being length-biased in a pure rank-then-fill baseline with no aggregation or search dynamics at all. Do not conflate the two mechanisms.

literature_comparison.note: docs/research/CODE_AUDIT_IEEE_Access.md's Table 6 records Lead/TextRank/LexRank as 'adopted from [16]', a different paper's pipeline (different preprocessing, sentence splitting, ROUGE settings, and possibly split) -- this is a directional sanity check only, NOT a validated apples-to-apples reproduction. See CLAUDE.md's global rule against treating cross-paper baseline numbers as a fair local comparison.

f19_textrank_run_log.description: Full tqdm log of the TextRank run backing runs_v2/textrank_val (this run was executed concurrently with the first lexrank attempt; its own internal time_select_seconds.txt is NOT confounded the same way lexrank's crash was, but see environment_note above for why timing from this log should not be quoted directly -- use the isolated calibration points in COMPUTE_ENVIRONMENT.md instead).

f19_lexrank_run_crash_log.description: The first LexRank attempt, aborted at validation_1082 (1082/5621, ~36 minutes in) under the pre-fix fail-loud-and-abort guard. Kept deliberately: this is F-17's original failure shape (one document's data characteristic destroying an entire batch's worth of completed work) recurring a third time in a code path F-17 never covered (after greedy's min_words and candidate_capacity_shortfall).

f19_lexrank_run2_isolated_success_log.description: The successful, isolated (no concurrent process) re-run backing runs_v2/lexrank_val, after the scorer_degenerate fix. time_select_seconds.txt (507.93s) matches this log's own tqdm elapsed almost exactly, confirming the earlier concurrent run's timing mismatch was a contention artifact, not broken instrumentation.

f19_lexrank_idf_collapse_scan_json.description: Full-split scan (5,621 docs, 456,942 sentences, 79.9s) checking, per document, whether every term's LexRank idf collapses to exactly 0 -- the actual necessary-and-sufficient trigger for the NaN guard (not the 'all-stopword sentence' misconception an earlier version of the guard's message assumed). Found exactly 2 hits (validation_1082, validation_2303), matching scorer_degenerate_rows above. Also records the misleading secondary signal (10,364 individual zero-effective-word sentences across 2,818 documents) that does NOT predict document-level collapse on its own.
